summary: Shows testing a module with ad hoc commands using ANSIBLE_LIBRARY or a collection FQCN with --playbook-dir, and running it directly with an args.json file (ANSIBLE_MODULE_ARGS) via python or python -m with PYTHONPATH set.
questions: How do I quickly test my new module with an ad hoc command?
How can I run my module directly with python for debugging?
What format does the module arguments file use?
How do I test a collection module without installing the collection?

answer_card.title: Test a module locally
answer_card.answer_md:
Ad hoc:
```shell
ANSIBLE_LIBRARY=./library ansible -m my_test -a 'name=hello new=true' localhost
ansible localhost -m my_namespace.my_collection.my_test -a 'name=hello new=true' --playbook-dir=$PWD
```
Direct (for pdb/print):
```json
{"ANSIBLE_MODULE_ARGS": {"name": "hello", "new": true}}
```
```console
python library/my_test.py /tmp/args.json
export PYTHONPATH=PATH_TO_COLLECTIONS:$PYTHONPATH
python -m ansible_collections.my_namespace.my_collection.plugins.modules.my_test /tmp/args.json
```
